title: Fairness Constraints: Mechanisms for Fair Classification
authors: Muhammad Bilal Zafar, Isabel Valera, Manuel Gomez Rodriguez, Krishna P. Gummadi
venue: Proceedings of the 20th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), PMLR vol. 54
conclusions: Introduces 'decision boundary covariance' between a sensitive attribute and the signed distance to the margin, as a convex, tractable proxy for the disparate-impact p%-rule.

Derives two convex formulations for margin-based classifiers (logistic regression, SVM): (i) maximize accuracy subject to a fairness (covariance) constraint, (ii) maximize fairness subject to an accuracy constraint (including a fine-grained per-point loss constraint for the 'business necessity' clause).
Sensitive attributes are excluded from the classifier's input features (avoids disparate treatment) while the covariance constraint on model outputs controls disparate impact (group-wise fairness).
Constraints are enforced during training via a convex constrained optimization (Lagrangian dual) formulation, not via pre/post-processing.
Handles binary, non-binary, and multiple sensitive attributes simultaneously, unlike most prior work compared in Table 1.

Experiments on synthetic data plus Adult and Bank real-world datasets show fine-grained, Pareto-optimal control of the fairness/accuracy trade-off, comparable to or better than preferential sampling and regularized logistic regression baselines.
